original_value: In the last 10 years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has seen successes in fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, robotics and autonomous systems. However, these advances are still considered as Narrow AI, i.e. AI built for very specific or constrained applications. These applications have its usefulness in improving the quality of human life; but it is not good enough to do highly general tasks like what the human can do. The holy grail of AI research is to develop Strong AI or Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), which produces human-level intelligence, i.e. the ability to sense, understand, reason, learn and act in dynamic environments. Strong AI is more than just a composition of Narrow AI technologies. We proposed that it has to be a holistic approach towards understanding and reacting to the operating environment and decision-making process. The Strong AI must be able to demonstrate sentience, emotional intelligence, imagination, effective command of other machines or robots, and self-referring and self-reflecting qualities. This paper will give an overview of current Narrow AI capabilities, present the technical gaps, and highlight future research directions for Strong AI. Could Strong AI become conscious? We provide some discussion pointers.

result.paraphrase: Over the past decade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has achieved notable results in areas including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, robotics, and autonomous systems. Even so, these developments are still viewed as Narrow AI, meaning AI designed for highly specific or limited uses. While such applications can improve the quality of human life, they are not sufficient for highly general tasks like those humans can perform. The central goal of AI research is to create Strong AI, or Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), capable of human-level intelligence—the ability to sense, understand, reason, learn, and act in dynamic environments. Strong AI is not merely a combination of Narrow AI technologies; we argue that it must take a holistic approach to understanding the operating environment and decision-making process. It should be able to show sentience, emotional intelligence, imagination, effective control of other machines or robots, and self-referential, self-reflective qualities. This paper surveys current Narrow AI capabilities, identifies technical gaps, and points to future research directions for Strong AI. Could Strong AI become conscious? We offer some discussion points.
